questions.question: Which of the following allows us to identify objects and extract information?
questions.explanation: RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification) identifies tagged objects by exchanging radio signals between a tag and a reader. The tag supplies an identifier or other stored information, so the system can recognize an item without relying on a person to inspect it visually. Sensors measure physical conditions such as temperature or pressure, while actuators cause actions; RFID is the option specifically designed for object identification.

questions.question: How many layers does Zigbee consist of?
questions.explanation: The introductory Zigbee stack is commonly presented as four layers: physical, MAC, network, and application. The physical layer handles radio transmission, the MAC layer manages access to the wireless channel, the network layer supports addressing and routing, and the application layer supplies services to devices. This four-layer description is the simplified model used in the question; it should not be confused with counting every sublayer in a broader protocol-stack diagram.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of cloud computing?
questions.explanation: In the component classification used by this question, clients, services, and applications are cloud-computing components, whereas “local servers” is not one of the listed standard components. Cloud services can run on physical servers, but the defining idea is that resources are offered as network-accessible services rather than being confined to a locally managed server. The question is testing that classification, not claiming that cloud infrastructure contains no servers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a distance measuring sensor module?
questions.explanation: The HC-SR04 is an ultrasonic ranging module: it emits a sound pulse and measures how long the echo takes to return from an object. Since the pulse travels to the object and back, the measured travel time is converted into distance. DHT22 measures temperature and humidity, TSL2591 measures light intensity, and HC-SR505 is a passive-infrared motion sensor, so these are not the intended distance-measuring module.

questions.question: Which of the following is a component in a typical sensor network?
questions.explanation: A typical sensor network may contain several kinds of supporting component. Sensor nodes collect measurements, a sink gathers readings from nodes, a gateway connects networks or translates between protocols, and routers forward packets toward their destinations. Since a sink, gateway, and router can all be components of a sensor-network deployment, “All of these” is the inclusive choice. Their exact roles may be combined in one device in some real systems.

questions.question: Which of the following sensors are responsible for measuring orientation and angular velocity?
questions.explanation: An accelerometer measures linear acceleration, GPS estimates location and movement, and a temperature sensor measures heat-related conditions. Orientation and angular velocity are commonly measured or estimated with a gyroscope and, for orientation, often by combining gyroscope and accelerometer data. Because a gyroscope is not listed, “None of these” is the best answer to the question as worded.

questions.question: "ISA 100.11A" is a wireless networking technology standard. ISA stands for _______.
questions.explanation: ISA is the International Society of Automation, the professional organization associated with the ISA-100.11a industrial wireless networking standard. The standard concerns wireless communication for automation and process-control environments, where reliable and secure data exchange between instruments and control systems matters. The other expansions in the options do not give the organization’s name.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a difference between traditional data center and cloud computing?
questions.explanation: Scalability, flexibility, and elasticity are commonly used to distinguish cloud computing from a traditional fixed-capacity data centre. Storage, however, exists in both environments, so it is not by itself a difference between them. The important contrast is how resources are provisioned, accessed, adjusted, and released—not whether data can be stored at all.

questions.question: Smart grid is also known as the energy internet.
questions.explanation: A smart grid combines electrical infrastructure with sensing, digital communication, and automated control. The term “energy internet” emphasizes that information can travel between utilities, consumers, and distributed energy resources, while electricity may flow in more than one direction—for example, from a rooftop solar installation back to the grid. It is therefore more connected and interactive than a purely one-way traditional grid.

questions.question: Can a point of node failure result in the partition of the network in the stationary sensor network?
questions.explanation: Yes. In a stationary sensor network, a node may be a critical bridge between two groups of nodes. If every path between those groups passes through that node, its failure can disconnect the network into separate components; in graph theory, such a node is often called an articulation point or cut vertex. Redundant paths can reduce this risk, but a stationary network does not automatically heal itself by moving nodes.

questions.question: According to the ITU Internet Report 2005 discussed in the lecture, the future Internet is expected to become wider and more complex mainly because:

options.text: Humans will completely stop using the Internet
Most Internet traffic may flow between devices and different kinds of things
Only desktop computers will remain connected
Internet communication will be restricted to email services

questions.correctOption: Most Internet traffic may flow between devices and different kinds of things
questions.explanation: The ITU Internet Report 2005 anticipated a future in which connected devices and everyday objects would generate and receive a substantial share of network traffic. This is the central idea behind the Internet of Things: communication is not limited to people browsing websites, but also includes machines exchanging measurements, status updates, and commands. The other options describe restrictions or outcomes that do not explain the expected growth in Internet complexity.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of IoT systems?

options.text: Presence of sleeping nodes, mobile nodes, and non-IP devices
Guaranteed continuous connectivity for every device at all times

questions.correctOption: Efficient and scalable architecture, Unambiguous naming and addressing, Presence of sleeping nodes, mobile nodes, and non-IP devices
questions.explanation: IoT systems need scalable architecture and clear naming/addressing so that many different devices can be identified and managed. They must also accommodate heterogeneous nodes, including sleeping devices, mobile devices, and devices that do not use IP natively. Continuous connectivity is not guaranteed: battery-powered sensors may sleep to save energy, and wireless links can be intermittent. Therefore A, B, and C are characteristics; D is not.

questions.question: In the lecture, "Smart Dust" refers to:

options.text: A cloud storage model for IoT data
A large-scale wireless router used in smart cities
Very tiny computing devices that can be sprayed or injected for sensing purposes
A type of IPv6 address used in IoT networks

questions.correctOption: Very tiny computing devices that can be sprayed or injected for sensing purposes
questions.explanation: Smart Dust refers to extremely small sensing and computing devices that can be deployed in large numbers to observe their surroundings. The concept imagines tiny units that can measure conditions such as chemicals in soil or other physical and biological signals. It is not a cloud-storage model, router, or address format; the defining idea is miniaturized sensing and computation distributed through an environment.

questions.question: Which statement best explains the relation between IoT and M2M communication?

options.text: IoT and M2M are exactly the same
M2M is broader than IoT because it includes people and applications
M2M is a part of IoT, while IoT has a broader scope of interactions
IoT does not include machine-to-machine interaction

questions.correctOption: M2M is a part of IoT, while IoT has a broader scope of interactions
questions.explanation: Machine-to-machine (M2M) communication focuses on devices exchanging data directly or through a network, often with little human involvement. The Internet of Things is broader: it can include M2M communication as well as people, applications, cloud platforms, services, and connected physical objects. Thus M2M is one part of the larger IoT ecosystem rather than a completely separate or identical concept.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In the Web of Things, IoT sensors are replaced completely by cloud databases.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because the Web of Things builds on IoT devices rather than replacing them. Sensors still gather information from the physical world, and actuators may still change that world in response to commands. Web technologies and common interfaces help make those devices easier to access and integrate. A cloud database may store or process readings, but it cannot replace the sensing role of the physical sensor itself.

questions.question: In an IoT network configuration, local addresses may be valid only within a gateway’s domain. The same local address may even appear under another gateway. The main advantage of this strategy is:

options.text: It removes the requirement of a gateway
It prevents any device from communicating with the Internet

questions.explanation: Allowing local addresses to be reused in separate gateway domains reduces the demand for globally unique addresses. A device’s local address only needs to be unique within its own local network or gateway domain, so another network can use the same local value without creating a conflict, provided gateways keep the domains distinct. This address reuse conserves the available address space; it does not remove the gateway or prevent Internet access.

questions.question: Which of the following functions are associated with IoT gateways in the addressing strategy discussed in the lecture?

options.text: Obtaining upstream address prefixes using mechanisms such as DHCPv6
Delegating addresses to nodes using SLAAC

questions.correctOption: Providing Internet connectivity, Supporting IoT LAN intra-connectivity, Obtaining upstream address prefixes using mechanisms such as DHCPv6, Delegating addresses to nodes using SLAAC
questions.explanation: An IoT gateway can connect the local IoT network to the Internet, support communication among devices on the local network, obtain an upstream IPv6 prefix through mechanisms such as DHCPv6, and help nodes form addresses using SLAAC. These functions allow constrained devices to use network addresses and communicate beyond their immediate link. Because all four listed roles are included in the addressing strategy described in the question, all four options apply.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about IPv6 compared to IPv4?

options.text: IPv6 has a smaller address space than IPv4
IPv6 uses hexadecimal notation and supports a much larger address space
IPv6 requires broadcast addresses in the same way as IPv4

questions.correctOption: IPv6 uses hexadecimal notation and supports a much larger address space
questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses conventionally written in dotted-decimal form, whereas IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses written in hexadecimal groups. The much larger IPv6 address space helps support the enormous number of devices expected in IoT deployments. IPv6 does not have a smaller address space, and it relies on multicast and anycast rather than using broadcast in the same way as IPv4.

questions.question: Which statement correctly represents the design expectation from a good sensor?

options.text: It should influence the measured property significantly
It should respond strongly to unrelated physical properties
It should be sensitive to the measured property and should not disturb it
It should always produce random output

questions.correctOption: It should be sensitive to the measured property and should not disturb it
questions.explanation: A good sensor should respond reliably to the physical property it is intended to measure, while minimizing sensitivity to unrelated properties and avoiding significant disturbance of the quantity being measured. For example, a temperature sensor should respond to temperature rather than producing large changes merely because of an unrelated factor. Random output or a sensor that substantially alters its target would make measurements unreliable.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sensor resolution are correct?

options.text: Sensor resolution is the smallest change that the sensor can detect
For a digital sensor, resolution is related to the smallest digital output change it can process
Sensor resolution and sensor accuracy always refer to exactly the same property
Sensor accuracy does not depend only on resolution

questions.correctOption: Sensor resolution is the smallest change that the sensor can detect, For a digital sensor, resolution is related to the smallest digital output change it can process, Sensor accuracy does not depend only on resolution
questions.explanation: Resolution describes the smallest change in an input that a sensor or measurement system can distinguish. In a digital system, this is related to the smallest output step represented by the conversion process. Accuracy is different: it describes how close a reading is to the true value and can be affected by calibration, bias, noise, and other errors. Therefore A, B, and D are correct, while resolution and accuracy are not interchangeable.

questions.question: State True or False. An accelerometer that measures acceleration along the x, y, and z coordinate axes is classified as a vector sensor.
questions.explanation: An accelerometer reports acceleration along axes such as x, y, and z. These components form a vector because acceleration has both magnitude and direction; the combined readings describe acceleration relative to the sensor’s coordinate frame. A scalar sensor, by contrast, reports a quantity described by magnitude alone, such as temperature. This is why the described three-axis accelerometer is classified as a vector sensor.

questions.question: A sensor gives different output for the same input value depending on whether that input was reached by increasing or decreasing the measured quantity. This error is called:
questions.explanation: Hysteresis occurs when a sensor gives different outputs for the same present input depending on the direction from which that input was approached. For example, a reading at a particular pressure may differ when pressure is rising than when it is falling. This dependence on the input’s recent history is not the same as quantization error, which comes from representing a continuous value in discrete steps.

questions.question: State True or False. A hydraulic actuator can produce considerable force because liquids are nearly incompressible.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. Hydraulic actuators transmit force through a liquid, which is nearly incompressible under ordinary operating conditions. Pressure applied to the fluid can therefore be transmitted through the system to a piston or other mechanism, producing substantial mechanical force. The actuator’s output still depends on the applied pressure and the area of the piston; incompressibility is the key reason force can be transferred effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about Shape Memory Polymer actuators?

options.text: They may respond to stimuli such as light, heat, electrical, magnetic, pH, or moisture changes
They can show high strain recovery
They may have properties such as low density and biocompatibility
They are used only as passive temperature sensors

questions.correctOption: They may respond to stimuli such as light, heat, electrical, magnetic, pH, or moisture changes, They can show high strain recovery, They may have properties such as low density and biocompatibility
questions.explanation: Shape Memory Polymer (SMP) actuators can change shape in response to a stimulus and then recover a programmed shape under suitable conditions. Depending on the material, stimuli may include heat, light, electricity, magnetic fields, pH, or moisture. SMPs may also offer low density, high recoverable strain, and biocompatibility. They are active materials used to produce motion or shape change, not merely passive temperature sensors, so A, B, and C are correct.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: According to the IoT implementation example discussed in the lecture, data gathered by a sensor travels through a gateway and a proxy server before arriving at the cloud server.
questions.explanation: The statement is true for the particular IoT implementation sequence described in the lecture: a sensor collects the measurement, a gateway provides local communication or protocol bridging, and a proxy server forwards the data onward before it reaches the cloud server. The cloud can then store, process, or present the readings. This describes the architecture in the example, rather than a mandatory route for every IoT design.

questions.question: In MQTT, which field of a published message is used by the broker as routing information?
questions.explanation: An MQTT publisher attaches a topic to each published message. The broker uses that topic to compare the message against subscribers’ topic filters and forwards the message to matching subscribers. A client identifier identifies a client session, while payload length and session timers do not define the destination for a publication. Topics therefore provide the routing information central to MQTT’s publish/subscribe model.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about MQTT topic wildcards are correct?

options.text: The plus sign (+) matches an arbitrary value at exactly one hierarchy level.
The hash sign (#) can be used to subscribe to all underlying hierarchy levels.
The subscription house/# matches only the exact topic house.
The subscription house/+/temperature can match house/kitchen/temperature.

questions.correctOption: The plus sign (+) matches an arbitrary value at exactly one hierarchy level., The hash sign (#) can be used to subscribe to all underlying hierarchy levels., The subscription house/+/temperature can match house/kitchen/temperature.
questions.explanation: MQTT uses topic wildcards to subscribe to groups of topics without listing every topic individually. The plus sign (+) matches exactly one hierarchy level, so `house/+/temperature` can match `house/kitchen/temperature`. The hash sign (#) matches multiple remaining levels and is normally placed at the end of a filter; `house/#` covers topics under the `house` hierarchy, not only the exact topic `house`. Therefore A, B, and D are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following are main stages of Secure MQTT (SMQTT)?
questions.explanation: The Secure MQTT (SMQTT) flow described in the lecture includes setup, encryption, publishing, and decryption. Setup establishes the relevant security context; encryption protects the message content; publishing sends the protected message through MQTT; and decryption allows the authorized recipient to recover it. Route discovery is a networking function and is not one of the four SMQTT stages. The listed answer includes the relevant stages offered among the options.

questions.question: At the transport layer, CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) operates over which protocol?
questions.explanation: CoAP is designed for constrained devices and low-overhead communication, so it commonly uses UDP rather than TCP at the transport layer. UDP avoids the connection-establishment and stream-management overhead of TCP, which can be useful for small messages and limited devices. CoAP adds its own message types and reliability mechanisms where needed. TCP, SCTP, and FTP are not the transport protocol specified by this question.

questions.question: State True or False. In CoAP, a piggyback response is carried with the acknowledgment, whereas in the separate mode, the server response is sent in a message separate from the acknowledgment.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. In CoAP piggyback mode, the server places the response in the acknowledgment to a confirmable request, avoiding a separate response message. In separate-response mode, the server acknowledges the request first and sends the response later in a distinct message, often because processing takes longer. The distinction is about whether the response accompanies the acknowledgment or arrives separately.

questions.question: Which of the following CoAP request-method mappings are correct?
questions.correctOption: GET - retrieve data, PUT - create data, PUSH - update data, DELETE - delete data
questions.explanation: CoAP’s standard request methods are GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE. GET retrieves a representation of a resource; POST submits data or requests an action and is often used to create a resource; PUT creates or replaces the state of a resource at a known URI; and DELETE removes a resource. The option uses “PUSH” rather than the standard method “POST,” so that wording should be checked against the source assignment: PUSH is not a standard CoAP request method. Do not use this item as a reliable methods reference until that label is corrected.

questions.question: Which AMQP frame type is used to control the message-flow rate?
questions.explanation: The AMQP Flow frame carries information used to manage link flow control, including how much message transfer a peer is currently prepared to accept. This helps avoid overwhelming a receiver and supports controlled transfer of messages between AMQP endpoints. Transfer carries message deliveries, Disposition communicates the outcome or state of a delivery, and Detach closes a link; those frames have different purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about AMQP components are correct?

options.text: An exchange receives messages and routes them to queues.
A queue stores messages for business processes or consumers.
A binding specifies message-distribution rules between an exchange and queues.
A consumer must route every producer message before it reaches an exchange.

questions.correctOption: An exchange receives messages and routes them to queues., A queue stores messages for business processes or consumers., A binding specifies message-distribution rules between an exchange and queues.
questions.explanation: AMQP separates message routing, storage, and routing rules. A producer sends a message to an exchange; the exchange evaluates routing rules and directs it to one or more queues; a queue holds messages until consumers receive them; and bindings connect an exchange to queues with the relevant distribution rules. Consumers process messages from queues rather than routing every producer message before it reaches an exchange. This makes A, B, and C correct.

questions.question: Which of the following IEEE 802.15.4 variant-application pairs are correct?
questions.correctOption: IEEE 802.15.4c - China, IEEE 802.15.4e - Industrial applications, IEEE 802.15.4f - Active RFID, IEEE 802.15.4g - Smart utility networks
questions.explanation: The variants address different application needs. IEEE 802.15.4c added regional options associated with China, 802.15.4e introduced MAC enhancements suited to industrial applications, 802.15.4f addressed active RFID, and 802.15.4g targeted smart utility networks. The suffixes matter because the amendments extend the base low-rate wireless personal-area-network standard for distinct regulatory or operational requirements. According to the pairings in the question, all four options are correct.

questions.question: In a non-beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 network, data frames are transmitted using:
questions.explanation: In a non-beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 network, devices use unslotted CSMA/CA to contend for the channel. A device senses the medium and follows the contention procedure before transmission, but it does not align its backoff periods to beacon-defined time slots. Beacon-enabled operation, by contrast, uses a coordinated superframe and slotted CSMA/CA. Token passing and pure TDMA are not the method specified here.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between IEEE 802.15.4 and ZigBee?

options.text: IEEE 802.15.4 provides layers 1 and 2, while ZigBee extends the functionality to layer 3 and above.
ZigBee provides only the physical layer, while IEEE 802.15.4 provides all higher layers.
Both standards operate only at the application layer.
ZigBee and IEEE 802.15.4 are identical standards with no functional distinction.

questions.correctOption: IEEE 802.15.4 provides layers 1 and 2, while ZigBee extends the functionality to layer 3 and above.
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.15.4 defines the lower layers—particularly the physical radio layer and MAC sublayer—used by low-rate wireless personal-area networks. ZigBee builds on those layers and supplies higher-level networking and application functionality, such as addressing, routing, and security services. The two standards therefore complement one another; they are not identical, and ZigBee does not replace the lower-layer specification.

questions.question: Which of the following statements characterizes a ZigBee end device?

options.text: It communicates with its parent node.
It cannot relay data for other devices.
It forms the network root and acts as the trust center.

questions.correctOption: It communicates with its parent node., It cannot relay data for other devices., It is a reduced-functionality device.
questions.explanation: A ZigBee end device communicates through its parent node and normally does not route or relay traffic for other nodes. This reduced-functionality role allows an end device to be simpler and often to conserve energy, since it does not need to maintain routing information for the network. Network formation and trust-center responsibilities belong to a coordinator or other designated network components, not to an ordinary end device. Thus A, B, and C describe an end device.

questions.question: Which option correctly describes addressing in 6LoWPAN?

options.text: A 16-bit address is globally unique, while a 64-bit address is PAN-specific.
A 16-bit short address is PAN-specific and assigned by the PAN coordinator, while a 64-bit extended address is globally unique.
Both 16-bit and 64-bit addresses are globally unique and assigned by an Internet router.
Both address types are used only for multicast communication.

questions.correctOption: A 16-bit short address is PAN-specific and assigned by the PAN coordinator, while a 64-bit extended address is globally unique.
questions.explanation: 6LoWPAN supports short and extended addressing in IEEE 802.15.4 networks. A 16-bit short address is assigned for use within a particular personal-area network (PAN), so it only needs to be unique there. A 64-bit extended address provides a much larger identifier space and is globally unique. The distinction allows compact local addressing while retaining a globally distinctive hardware identifier.

questions.question: State True or False. In LOADng routing, an intermediate router may respond to a Route Request (RREQ) whenever it already has an active route to the requested destination.
questions.explanation: The statement is false under the LOADng routing rule described in the assignment. When a node needs a route, it broadcasts a Route Request (RREQ); in the described protocol, the destination responds to that request. An intermediate router does not reply merely because it already has an active route to the destination. That restriction distinguishes the stated LOADng behavior from protocols that permit intermediate replies.

questions.question: How does a passive RFID tag obtain the power required to transmit information?

options.text: It uses its own internal battery.
It is powered inductively by an RFID reader.
It receives power through a wired AIDC connection.
It does not require any source of power.

questions.correctOption: It is powered inductively by an RFID reader.
questions.explanation: A passive RFID tag does not carry its own battery for normal operation. The reader emits an electromagnetic field; the tag couples to that field—inductively at the appropriate frequencies—and harvests enough energy to power its circuit and reply. Active tags differ because they have an internal power source. Therefore, a passive tag can communicate without a battery, but it still requires energy supplied by the reader’s field.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: There is no network layer in Wired HART
questions.explanation: The statement is true according to the Wired HART architecture described in the lecture: Wired HART does not define a separate network layer in the same way as a full general-purpose network stack. Its communication design is focused on industrial instrumentation and the protocol layers needed to exchange data between field devices and control systems. The answer is about the specific HART stack taught in the course, not a claim that all industrial networks lack network layers.

questions.question: Zwave operates at ______ MHz in the US and ______ MHz in Europe.
questions.explanation: The frequencies specified in the question are 908.42 MHz in the United States and 868.42 MHz in Europe. Z-Wave uses region-specific sub-GHz bands because radio spectrum allocations differ by country or region. Using the appropriate band is necessary for regulatory compliance and interoperability; a device designed for one region may not work correctly or legally in another.

questions.question: Dumb behavior of sensor nodes is __________ in nature (as it is dependent on the effects of the environmental conditions).
questions.explanation: The lecture describes this sensor-node behavior as temporal because it changes over time in response to environmental conditions. A node’s sensing or communication behavior may need to vary as conditions evolve, rather than depending only on where the node is located. “Spatial” would describe variation by location; the question explicitly emphasizes dependence on environmental effects over time, making temporal the intended answer.

questions.question: The process of identifying channels consistently affected by interference and removing them from use is known as
questions.explanation: The named procedure is channel blacklisting: channels that are repeatedly degraded by interference are identified and excluded from normal use. This helps a wireless system avoid repeatedly transmitting over unreliable frequencies. Since “Channel Trimming” and “Channel Flushing” are not the name used for that procedure in the lecture, none of the listed alternatives gives the correct term.

questions.question: The full form of NFC is
questions.explanation: NFC stands for Near Field Communication. It is a short-range wireless communication technology that allows compatible devices or tags to exchange information when brought close together. It is used in applications such as contactless access, product information, and tap-to-pair interactions. “Near Field Contact” is not the correct expansion, so the communication option is the accurate one.

questions.question: State true or false. NFC works on the principle of magnetic induction.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. NFC commonly relies on near-field electromagnetic coupling, often described through magnetic induction between a reader and a nearby tag or device. The reader’s alternating field can transfer data and, for passive tags, provide operating energy. The short operating distance is part of the technology’s design and helps support deliberate tap-like interactions.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: NFC tags found in supermarket products are examples of active NFC.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because tags used in common product-identification examples are typically passive, not active. A passive tag obtains energy from the reader’s field and responds without needing its own battery. An active tag has its own power source and may communicate over a greater range. The question is distinguishing the usual tag type from supermarket-style NFC/RFID use, not saying that active tags never exist.

questions.question: Bluetooth is based on
questions.explanation: The correct underlying term is piconet. Bluetooth devices form a small ad-hoc network, commonly called a piconet, in which one device coordinates communication with other participating devices. “Nanonets” and “Binarynets” are not the standard Bluetooth network terminology, and neither option accurately names the arrangement. Therefore, among the listed choices, “None of these” is correct.

questions.question: A ______ in NFC emits a small electric current which creates a magnetic field that in turn bridges the physical space between the devices.
questions.explanation: In an NFC reader, an alternating electrical current in the antenna creates a magnetic field. A nearby compatible device or tag couples to this field, enabling communication across the small physical gap without a wired connection. For passive tags, the field can also supply energy to the tag circuitry. The reader is therefore the component that initiates the field in the described interaction.

questions.question: State true of false. Bluetooth technology is based on Ad-hoc network technology.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. Bluetooth is designed to allow nearby devices to establish links and exchange data without requiring a fixed wired infrastructure, which is a characteristic of ad-hoc networking. Devices can form connections for uses such as audio, peripherals, and data exchange. Although a Bluetooth network may be coordinated by a central device, that does not make it a fixed infrastructure network.

questions.question: State true or false. Zwave utilizes GFSK modulation and Hongkong channel encoding.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because the channel encoding identified in the lecture is Manchester encoding, not “Hongkong channel encoding.” GFSK—Gaussian Frequency Shift Keying—is a modulation method used by Z-Wave, while encoding defines how bits are represented in the transmitted signal. These are related but distinct parts of the physical communication system, so the incorrect encoding name makes the whole statement false.

questions.question: The process of bypassing radio dead-spots is done using a message called in Zwave.
questions.explanation: Z-Wave healing refers to the network’s ability to refresh or adjust routing when communication paths are unreliable, helping nodes route around radio dead spots. This is important in buildings where walls, interference, or device placement can make a previously valid route fail. The idea is route recovery rather than a generic ping or an ordinary data frame, so “Healing” is the intended option.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: Sensor nodes have unlimited battery life.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because wireless sensor nodes generally run on limited battery energy. Radio communication, sensing, computation, and frequent retransmissions all consume power, and replacing or recharging batteries may be difficult in remote deployments. Network protocols often use sleep schedules, efficient messages, and energy-aware routing to extend operating life; unlimited battery life is not a realistic design assumption.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: The Link Manager Protocol in Bluetooth manages the establishment, authentication, link configuration.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. Bluetooth’s Link Manager Protocol (LMP) handles link-level control tasks between devices, including link establishment, authentication, and configuration of link parameters. It coordinates aspects of the Bluetooth connection that allow the devices to establish and maintain a usable link. This is different from the application layer, which defines what the connected devices do with the exchanged data.

questions.question: Zigbee commonly uses ______ data rate.
questions.explanation: ZigBee commonly supports a raw data rate of 250 kbps in the 2.4 GHz band. This relatively modest rate is intentional: ZigBee is designed for low-power, low-cost monitoring and control rather than high-throughput media. The protocol family is useful for sensors, home automation, and other devices that send short messages and need long battery life. Mbps-scale options in the list are far too high for the stated standard rate.

questions.question: What does the ultrasonic sensor measure generally in the AID system?
questions.explanation: In the Agricultural Intrusion Detection (AID) system, the ultrasonic sensor is used as a range sensor. It sends an ultrasonic pulse and uses the returning echo to estimate how far away the detected object is. That distance helps the system determine whether something has entered the monitored area. Humidity, soil pH, and light intensity require different sensing elements, so they are not the function assigned to the ultrasonic sensor here.

questions.question: Which component processes the data received from the sensors in the AID system?
questions.explanation: The microcontroller receives measurements from the sensors and runs the logic that interprets them. It can compare readings with thresholds, decide whether an intrusion condition has been detected, and coordinate a response or communication to another component. A camera or ultrasonic sensor supplies data rather than serving as the central data-processing unit, while an NFC tag is an identification device rather than the controller.

questions.question: How can standard nanodevices communicate?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies electromagnetic and molecular communication as approaches for standard nanodevices. Electromagnetic methods use signals associated with electromagnetic fields, whereas molecular communication represents information through molecules or chemical signals. Wired Ethernet and ZigBee are conventional networking technologies designed for much larger devices and different physical assumptions, so they are not the communication modes selected for nanodevices in this question.

questions.question: When does sensing coverage guarantee network connectivity?

options.text: When the transmission range is at least twice the sensing range
When the sensing range is at least twice the transmission range
When the transmission and sensing ranges are equal
When the transmission range is smaller than the sensing range

questions.correctOption: When the transmission range is at least twice the sensing range
questions.explanation: For the coverage-to-connectivity guarantee stated in the lecture, the transmission range must be at least twice the sensing range. Sensing range tells how far a node can observe a target; transmission range tells how far it can communicate with another node. If communication reaches sufficiently farther than sensing, the overlap needed to cover the monitored area also supports connected communication among the sensing nodes under the stated model.

questions.question: Which of the following is a coverage problem in a static WSN?
questions.explanation: Area coverage asks whether the sensing regions of deployed nodes adequately cover a target area. It is a core problem in a static wireless sensor network because nodes need to monitor the required space without leaving blind spots or deploying unnecessary redundant nodes. Data compression, route encryption, and clock synchronization are useful network functions, but they are not coverage-problem categories.

questions.question: Which reporting method is used for forest-fire monitoring in a WSN?
questions.explanation: Forest-fire monitoring is naturally event-driven: sensor nodes send reports when measurements indicate a relevant event, such as a sudden rise in temperature or smoke-related condition. This can reduce unnecessary traffic compared with continuously transmitting every reading. On-demand reporting is more suitable when a user or application requests information, while manual reporting relies on a person rather than automatic event detection.

questions.question: What does a data mule do?

options.text: Collects data and carries it to the sink

questions.correctOption: Collects data and carries it to the sink
questions.explanation: A data mule is a mobile carrier—such as a vehicle, robot, or person—that visits sensor nodes, collects stored readings, and later carries those readings to a sink or gateway. It is especially useful when sensors have limited connectivity or direct long-range transmission would consume too much energy. The data mule does not replace all sensors or repair hardware; its role is to move collected information between locations.

questions.question: What may happen if a critical stationary sensor node fails?

options.text: The network repairs itself by movement

questions.explanation: A stationary sensor node can be important because it connects neighboring nodes or two otherwise separate parts of the network. If that critical node fails and no alternate route exists, packets can no longer cross between those parts, effectively partitioning the network. The sensing range does not automatically increase and stationary devices do not move to fix the problem. Redundant connectivity is one way to reduce the risk.

questions.question: A person who provides sensing information acts as a:
questions.explanation: In human-centric sensing, a person may contribute information by observing, reporting, or carrying a device that collects measurements. In that role, the person or their device is a data source: it provides input to the sensing system. A router forwards packets, a radio channel carries signals, and an actuator performs an action, so those alternatives do not describe the information-providing role asked about here.

questions.question: Which is an advantage of a stationary wireless sensor network?
questions.explanation: Stationary sensor nodes remain at known, fixed locations, so their positions and links are generally easier to model and maintain than those in a mobile network. Once the deployment is planned, routing and coverage can be assessed without constantly adapting to movement. A stationary network cannot automatically move a node after failure, and its topology does not change merely because node locations are unpredictable.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In a UAV network, the network topology may change frequently because the UAVs are mobile.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. UAVs move through space, so the distances and relative positions between them change with time. A movement may create a new wireless link or take a node out of another node’s communication range, requiring routing and connectivity to adapt. This frequent change in topology is a defining challenge for UAV networks and makes robust, rapidly updated networking particularly important.

questions.question: Which is a common issue in UAV networks?
questions.explanation: Frequent topology changes are a common challenge in UAV networks because aircraft move and can rapidly alter which nodes can communicate directly. Links may appear, disappear, or vary in quality, which can invalidate routes and interrupt data delivery. Fixed positions and permanent communication links are therefore unrealistic assumptions, and UAV failures remain possible in practical deployments.

questions.question: Compared with traditional SCADA, M2M supports:
questions.explanation: M2M systems can connect devices and software from different platforms, allowing machines to exchange information across equipment or application boundaries. Traditional SCADA deployments have often been built around specialized, relatively isolated control systems, although modern SCADA can also be networked. The intended advantage here is cross-platform integration: it lets data from different systems be combined instead of remaining trapped in a single proprietary environment.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In a stationary wireless sensor network, sensor nodes can automatically move to restore connectivity after a node failure.
questions.explanation: The statement is false. A stationary wireless sensor network is made up of nodes that remain in their deployed locations; they do not move themselves to repair network connectivity after another node fails. Connectivity may be restored through an alternate route if one exists, or by human intervention or a separate mobile device, but automatic relocation is not a property of the stationary network model.

questions.question: Which statement best describes M2M communication?

options.text: Devices can exchange data without direct human control
Every data exchange must be performed manually
Only one device can communicate at a time
Devices cannot communicate through a network

questions.correctOption: Devices can exchange data without direct human control
questions.explanation: Machine-to-machine (M2M) communication allows devices to exchange data automatically over a wired or wireless connection with little or no direct human action for each exchange. For example, a sensor can send readings to a controller, which can respond based on a rule. People may still configure, supervise, and maintain the system, but individual messages do not need to be sent manually.

questions.question: What does interoperability allow IoT devices to do?
questions.explanation: Interoperability means that devices or systems built with different hardware, software, or communication protocols can still exchange data and work together. In an IoT deployment, this allows sensors from one vendor to provide readings to a platform from another vendor rather than forcing the entire system to use one device type. Interoperability does not require devices to work offline or disable each other; it makes coordinated operation possible.

questions.question: Syntactic interoperability deals with:
questions.explanation: Syntactic interoperability concerns the structure and format of exchanged information—for example, whether two systems encode a message as JSON, XML, or a defined field layout that both sides can parse. It does not mean that the devices have matching physical properties such as battery size, colour, or weight. If systems agree on syntax, the receiver can interpret the message structure, even though semantic agreement about what the values mean is a separate concern.

questions.question: What does UMB stand for?
questions.explanation: UMB stands for Universal Middleware Bridge in the terminology used by this course. A middleware bridge helps otherwise different middleware systems or devices interoperate by mediating between their interfaces or communication conventions. The idea is to let components work together without requiring every device to be rebuilt around one identical platform. The other options are not the expansion given for UMB in the lecture.

questions.question: What is the operating voltage of the Arduino UNO?
questions.explanation: The Arduino UNO is built around a 5 V operating logic supply in the standard board version described by the lecture. Its digital pins and common examples are therefore generally discussed using 5 V logic, although some board revisions and connected peripherals have their own voltage limits that should always be checked. The other values are not the operating voltage specified for the Arduino UNO in this question.

questions.question: What is a program written in the Arduino IDE called?
questions.explanation: A program written in the Arduino IDE is called a sketch. A sketch usually contains setup() for one-time initialization and loop() for code that runs repeatedly while the board is powered. The IDE compiles the sketch and uploads it to the Arduino. “Packet” and “frame” refer to data units used in communication, while “query” is not the Arduino IDE term for a program.

questions.question: Which interface is mainly used to connect an Arduino UNO to a computer?
questions.explanation: The Arduino UNO is typically connected to a computer using USB. The USB connection allows the IDE to upload the compiled sketch and can also supply power during development, depending on the setup. HDMI and VGA are display interfaces, while Ethernet is a networking interface and is not the standard direct programming connection on the UNO board described here.

questions.question: What is the conventional starting index of an array in Arduino programming?
questions.explanation: Arduino arrays use zero-based indexing, as does C/C++: the first element is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so forth. For an array of length n, valid indices typically run from 0 to n−1. Remembering this avoids off-by-one errors when reading or writing an element. Index −1 is not the first element in normal Arduino array indexing.

questions.question: Which Arduino function is used to generate a pseudo-random number within a specified range?
questions.explanation: The random() function generates pseudo-random integer values for use in a sketch, such as selecting a delay or choosing among behaviours. Its range depends on the arguments: random(max) returns a value from 0 up to but not including max, and random(min, max) uses the specified lower bound and exclusive upper bound. The other options configure pins, write digital outputs, or manage interrupts; they do not generate random values.

questions.question: In the traffic-control example, which LED is switched ON first to represent the GO signal?
questions.explanation: In the traffic-signal example, the green LED is switched on first to represent the GO signal. The program then waits for the programmed interval and advances through the other light states—typically yellow and then red—to model the traffic-light sequence. This question checks the order of the specific sketch, not a universal requirement that all real traffic controllers must begin at green after startup.

questions.question: Which quantities are measured by a DHT sensor?
questions.explanation: A DHT sensor is designed to measure temperature and relative humidity. Its readings can be used in environmental monitoring or control systems, such as switching a fan on when a room or device becomes too warm. It does not measure distance, speed, light, sound, pressure, or altitude; those quantities require different sensor types.

questions.question: What does a sensor convert a physical quantity into?
questions.explanation: A sensor converts a physical quantity—such as temperature, pressure, light, or motion—into an electrical signal that an electronic system can read and process. The signal may be a voltage, current, resistance change, pulse, or digital data depending on the sensor design. The resulting measurement can then be interpreted by a microcontroller or other system. A sensor does not itself convert the measurement into a software program, motion, or a network address.

questions.question: In the DHT sensor sketch, delay(2000) causes successive readings to be printed after approximately how much time?
questions.explanation: In Arduino and Python-style timing examples, delay(2000) represents 2,000 milliseconds. Since 1,000 milliseconds equal one second, 2,000 milliseconds correspond to approximately two seconds between successive readings, assuming the rest of the loop adds negligible time. The argument is not measured in seconds, so 2000 should not be interpreted as 2,000 seconds or 0.2 seconds.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A servo motor is a low-precision motor used only for linear motion.
questions.explanation: The statement is false. A servo motor is designed to control position or movement with feedback or a defined position-control mechanism, and it is widely used where controlled angular motion is needed. It is not accurately described as a low-precision device used only for linear motion. Servos commonly provide rotary movement, and their achievable precision depends on the servo design and control system.

questions.question: Which device provides controlled rotary motion?
questions.explanation: A servo motor is an actuator because it converts an electrical control signal and supplied energy into mechanical motion. In common hobby and robotics applications, it rotates to a commanded angle within its operating range, making it useful for steering, positioning, and mechanisms that need controlled movement. Ultrasonic, DHT, and PIR devices are sensors; they measure distance, temperature/humidity, or motion rather than providing the controlled rotary output.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A stepper motor is a type of actuator.
questions.explanation: A stepper motor is an actuator because it converts electrical pulses into discrete mechanical steps. By controlling the number and sequence of pulses, a controller can move the shaft through a selected angle, which is useful for positioning applications such as small CNC equipment and robotics. It produces motion rather than measuring a physical quantity, so it belongs to the actuator category.

questions.question: What are the five basic data types available in Python, as introduced in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The five groups listed in the lecture are Numbers, Strings, Lists, Tuples, and Dictionaries. Numbers represent numeric values; strings store text; lists and tuples hold ordered collections, with lists being mutable and tuples generally immutable; dictionaries store key–value pairs. Python has additional types, such as sets and booleans, but this question asks for the five groups used in the course introduction.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
questions.explanation: Python uses the keyword def to begin a function definition. It is followed by the function name, parentheses containing any parameters, and a colon; the indented block beneath it contains the function body. For example, `def add(a, b):` begins a function that could return the sum of its arguments. The words func, define, and function are not Python keywords for defining a function.

questions.question: In Python's exception handling, which keyword is used to handle an exception raised inside the try block?
questions.explanation: Python handles exceptions with try and except blocks. Code that may fail is placed in the try block, and if a matching exception occurs, the associated except block can handle it rather than letting the error terminate the program unexpectedly. The `catch` keyword is used in some other languages, but Python uses `except`; `handle` and `rescue` are not the relevant Python keywords.

questions.question: Which mode of Python's open() function is used to add data to the end of an existing file without erasing its existing content?
questions.explanation: Append mode, written as `a`, adds new content to the end of a file instead of replacing the existing content. By contrast, `w` opens a file for writing and normally truncates its previous contents, while `r` is for reading. Use append mode for logs or data records that need to accumulate over time. The exact mode string matters because choosing write mode accidentally can erase data.

questions.question: Which Python library, installable via pip, is used for image read/write operations as covered in the lecture?
questions.explanation: PIL is the historical Python Imaging Library name; Pillow is the maintained, installable fork commonly used in modern Python projects. It supports opening, inspecting, transforming, and saving image files in many formats. NumPy focuses on numerical arrays, OpenCV is a broader computer-vision library, and Matplotlib is mainly used for visualization and plotting, so Pillow is the library most directly associated with basic image read/write operations in this question.

questions.question: Which socket_type value is used while creating a TCP/IP socket in Python's socket module?
questions.explanation: For a TCP connection in Python, the usual socket type is `SOCK_STREAM`, normally combined with the IPv4 address family `AF_INET` when using IPv4. TCP provides a connection-oriented byte stream with ordered, reliable delivery. `SOCK_DGRAM` is normally used for UDP datagrams, while raw and sequenced-packet sockets serve different purposes. The socket type specifies the communication semantics rather than the IP address itself.

questions.question: How many GPIO pins does the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B have, as shown in the specifications table?
questions.explanation: The Raspberry Pi 3 Model B uses a 40-pin GPIO header. GPIO pins provide digital input/output and selected alternate functions for communicating with components such as LEDs, switches, and sensors. The number refers to the physical header pins, not the number of pins that are all interchangeable as general-purpose inputs or outputs; some pins serve power, ground, or special functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an officially supported operating system for Raspberry Pi mentioned in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Raspbian—now commonly known as Raspberry Pi OS—is the operating system associated with the Raspberry Pi in the lecture. It is a Linux-based system designed for the board’s hardware and supports development tools, GPIO access, and common applications. Windows XP, macOS, and Solaris are not the officially supported Raspberry Pi operating-system choice identified in this question. Exact support varies by board generation and date, but Raspbian is the course answer.

questions.question: Raspberry Pi is best described as a:
questions.explanation: The Raspberry Pi is a single-board computer: its processor, memory, input/output connections, and other core computer functions are assembled on one compact board. With an operating system and peripherals, it can run programs and interact with sensors, cameras, networks, and actuators. It is not itself a printer or a smartphone, and although it can be configured for networking tasks, a Wi-Fi router is not its defining category.

questions.question: Which command is used to install the GPIO library on Raspberry Pi before programming the blinking LED example?
questions.explanation: The command `sudo apt-get install python-rpi.gpio` installs the RPi.GPIO library through the Raspberry Pi’s package manager in the environment described by the lecture. The library lets Python programs configure GPIO pins and read or drive them—for example, to blink an LED. The command requires appropriate permissions and applies to the older package setup in the lecture; current Raspberry Pi OS versions may use different package recommendations or Python environments.

questions.question: Where is the CSI camera connector slot located on the Raspberry Pi board?

options.text: Between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port
Next to the power supply pin
On the underside of the board

questions.correctOption: Between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port
questions.explanation: On the Raspberry Pi board shown in the lecture, the CSI camera connector is located between the Ethernet and HDMI ports. CSI stands for Camera Serial Interface and provides a dedicated connector for compatible camera modules. It is different from USB ports used for general peripherals and from the GPIO header used for low-level electronic interfaces; correctly identifying the connector helps avoid attaching a camera to the wrong interface.

questions.question: Which terminal command captures a still image using the Raspberry Pi camera?
questions.explanation: The command `raspistill -o image.jpg` is the command shown in the lecture for capturing a still image and writing it to a file named `image.jpg`. The `-o` argument specifies the output filename. This is a legacy Raspberry Pi camera command associated with older camera software stacks; newer Raspberry Pi OS releases may use `rpicam-still` instead, but the expected answer for the lecture example is `raspistill -o image.jpg`.

questions.question: What does DHT stand for in the DHT sensor used with Raspberry Pi in the auto-cooling system?
questions.explanation: In the lecture, DHT is expanded as Digital Humidity and Temperature. DHT sensors provide digital readings for environmental humidity and temperature through a data pin, alongside power and ground connections. The exact pin arrangement varies by sensor and module, and users should follow the specific datasheet, but the key concept is that the device provides both temperature and humidity measurements for monitoring or control.

questions.question: How many output terminals does the relay used in the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system have, as shown in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The relay shown in the example has three switching terminals: normally open (NO), common (COM), and normally closed (NC). When the relay is not energized, COM is connected to NC; when energized, the contact changes so COM connects to NO. This allows a low-power controller to switch another circuit. The three terminals are contact outputs and should not be confused with the relay’s coil connections.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system, the fan operates when the surrounding temperature rises above the threshold value specified in the code.
questions.explanation: The statement is true for the control logic described in the lecture. The program compares the temperature measured by the DHT sensor with a threshold value; when the reading rises above that threshold, it activates the relay or control output so that the fan runs. This is a simple feedback-based automation example. A practical implementation should also account for sensor errors, sensible hysteresis, and safe electrical switching.

questions.question: In the remote data logging system, which socket type is used to send sensor data from the client to the server?
questions.explanation: The remote data-logging example uses `SOCK_DGRAM`, which is the socket type normally used with UDP. UDP sends independent datagrams without establishing a TCP-style connection, making it a lightweight option for transmitting sensor readings. The corresponding socket call uses an address family such as `AF_INET` and the datagram type. `SOCK_STREAM` is normally associated with TCP, while the other types are not used for this simple client-to-server example.

questions.question: Which Adafruit function is used in the client code to read humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor?
questions.explanation: The client uses `Adafruit_DHT.read_retry()` to read humidity and temperature from the connected DHT sensor. The function attempts to obtain a valid reading and retries when necessary, which is helpful because sensor timing and communication can occasionally produce an invalid sample. The returned values can then be packaged and sent to the server. The other options are not the function name used by the Adafruit DHT library in the example.

questions.question: Where does the server in the remote data logging example save the data received from the client as mentioned in the lecture?

options.text: In a text file named Datalog.txt

questions.correctOption: In a text file named Datalog.txt
questions.explanation: In the lecture’s server example, incoming sensor readings are appended to a text file named `Datalog.txt`. Opening the file in append mode preserves earlier records and places each new received message at the end, making the file a simple log of the measurements over time. This example does not save directly to MySQL, an Excel spreadsheet, or a cloud dashboard; it demonstrates basic persistent logging to a local text file.

questions.question: Which Python string function is used to split the comma-separated sensor data into separate values on the server?
questions.explanation: Python’s `split()` method divides a string into pieces using a specified delimiter. For comma-separated sensor data, `data.split(',')` returns a list of fields separated at each comma, allowing the server to extract values such as temperature and humidity individually. `partition()` splits only around the first occurrence of a separator, while `divide()` and `separate()` are not string methods used for this purpose.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: Matplotlib Python library is used to plot the temperature and humidity data received at the server in the lecture.
questions.explanation: The statement is true. Matplotlib is a Python plotting library that can display received sensor measurements, for example by plotting temperature and humidity against time. Functions such as `plot()`, `xlabel()`, `ylabel()`, and `title()` help construct and label the graph. Visualizing the values makes trends, spikes, and changes easier to interpret than reading a stream of raw numbers from the server log.

questions.question: Which matplotlib function turns on interactive mode so that the plot updates in real time as new data arrives?
questions.explanation: Matplotlib’s `ion()` function turns on interactive mode. In this mode, a program can update a figure repeatedly while it continues running, which is useful for displaying new sensor readings as they arrive. It does not create a grid or subplot by itself: `grid()` configures grid lines, `subplot()` selects part of a figure, and `figure()` creates or selects a figure. Interactive mode still requires the code to update and redraw the plot appropriately.

questions.question: In a traditional (non-SDN) network, where does the routing protocol logic (e.g., OSPF) mainly execute?
questions.explanation: In a traditional non-SDN network, routing protocols such as OSPF generally run in the individual network devices. Each switch or router participates in protocol operation and maintains the information needed for forwarding, so control logic is distributed across the network. SDN changes this arrangement by separating the control logic from packet-forwarding devices and using a controller to manage forwarding decisions through interfaces such as OpenFlow.

questions.question: In which year was the OpenFlow project — from which the idea of software-defined networking originated — presented at ACM SIGCOMM?
questions.explanation: The OpenFlow project was presented at ACM SIGCOMM in 2008, an important milestone in the development of software-defined networking. OpenFlow provided a way for a controller to program flow entries in compatible switches, helping separate control decisions from the forwarding hardware. The date is a historical fact from the lecture; Stanford’s OpenFlow 1.0.0 specification followed in 2009 according to the source material.

questions.question: What message does a switch send to the SDN controller when it receives a packet for which no matching flow-rule exists?
questions.explanation: When an SDN switch receives a packet that does not match any installed flow rule, it can send a PACKET-IN message to the controller. The controller examines the packet and policy context, decides how it should be handled, and may install a new rule so similar future packets can be processed directly by the switch. This lets the network adapt without requiring every forwarding decision to be hard-coded in each switch.

questions.question: Which SDN API is used for communication between the control layer and the infrastructure layer?
questions.explanation: The southbound API connects the SDN control layer to the infrastructure or data plane, allowing the controller to communicate instructions and receive information from switches and other forwarding devices. OpenFlow is a well-known example of a southbound protocol. The northbound API is used by applications to communicate with the controller, while east-west interfaces commonly support communication between controllers.

questions.question: According to the lecture, approximately how many requests per second can a typical SDN controller handle through a single thread?
questions.explanation: The lecture gives approximately 200 requests per second as the capacity of a typical SDN controller using a single thread. This should be understood as a teaching-example estimate under the assumed conditions, not a universal performance limit for every controller. Actual throughput depends on hardware, implementation, workload, message complexity, and whether processing is parallelized across multiple threads or machines.

questions.question: Which control mechanism is described where the entire network's control decisions are taken by a single controller?
questions.explanation: Centralized control means that a single controller makes the network-wide control decisions in the model described by the question. This can provide a consistent view of network state and make policies easier to coordinate, although it can introduce scaling and resilience considerations. Distributed control places decision-making across multiple devices or controllers. Hierarchical and federated approaches use other arrangements rather than relying on only one central decision-maker.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a benefit of integrating SDN with IoT?
questions.explanation: Integrating SDN with IoT can improve visibility of network resources because a controller can collect information about switches, links, flows, and traffic patterns in a more coordinated way. This network-wide view can support routing choices and traffic analysis for IoT devices. The goal is better observability and management, not higher hardware costs, lower sensor accuracy, or removal of every controller.

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is a key resource-constraint challenge in wireless sensor networks that motivates software-defined WSN?
questions.explanation: Wireless sensor nodes have limited memory, processing capacity, and energy, so they cannot necessarily store and execute large amounts of control software. This constraint motivates designs such as software-defined WSNs, where more control logic can be managed externally and nodes execute relatively lightweight forwarding behavior. The other options describe resources that are not typical of constrained sensors: they do not have excess bandwidth or unlimited computation power.

questions.question: In the SDN-WISE protocol stack for sensor nodes, what does "INPP" stand for?
questions.explanation: INPP stands for In Network Packet Processing in the SDN-WISE protocol stack described in the lecture. It concerns how sensor nodes process packets and apply the forwarding behavior programmed through flow rules. By supporting programmable packet handling at constrained nodes, SDN-WISE can enable network control without requiring every node to run a large general-purpose networking stack. The other expansions are not the term used in the course.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a problem in traditional (non-SDN) mobile networks?

options.text: Difficult to scale due to static, over-provisioned networks

questions.correctOption: Difficult to scale due to static, over-provisioned networks
questions.explanation: Traditional mobile networks can be difficult to scale because their hardware and network configuration may be relatively static and over-provisioned for expected demand. Traffic patterns change, especially as mobile users move, and rigid provisioning can make capacity expensive or slow to adapt. Software-defined networking aims to make control more programmable and responsive. The other choices describe benefits or unrealistic conditions rather than the limitation identified in the lecture.

questions.question: In the ODIN architecture for software-defined wireless networks, what does the 'Odin agent' do?

options.text: It is placed at the controller end to manage policies
It replaces the OpenFlow protocol entirely
It is placed with the physical devices to communicate with the controller
It performs billing for cloud resources

questions.correctOption: It is placed with the physical devices to communicate with the controller
questions.explanation: In the ODIN architecture, an Odin agent is placed at the access point or with the physical wireless device so it can communicate with the controller. The Odin master resides on the controller side and coordinates the network’s policy and management. This division lets the controller influence wireless-network behavior through agents near the devices; the agent does not replace OpenFlow entirely or perform cloud billing.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Mobi-Flow's proactive rule placement approach in Software-Defined IoT?

options.text: To place flow-rules randomly across all access points
To predict users' future location and place flow-rules at APs accordingly
To eliminate the need for a controller
To increase the number of PACKET-IN messages

questions.correctOption: To predict users' future location and place flow-rules at APs accordingly
questions.explanation: Mobi-Flow uses prediction to anticipate where users are likely to move and proactively places flow rules at access points associated with those future locations. By preparing the network before a user arrives, it can reduce the delay of waiting for a packet miss and a new controller decision. The described approach uses an order-K Markov predictor; it does not place rules randomly, eliminate the controller, or aim to increase PACKET-IN traffic.

questions.question: Which simulation tool is mentioned in the lecture for experimenting with wireless software-defined networks, supporting both wired and wireless (IEEE 802.11) protocols?
questions.explanation: Mininet-WiFi extends the Mininet network-emulation approach to support wireless network experiments, including IEEE 802.11 links, while also allowing wired Ethernet components. This is useful for prototyping and evaluating software-defined wireless topologies without requiring a full physical deployment. CloudSim and GreenCloud focus on cloud-system simulation, while NS2 is a different network simulator and is not the specific tool named in this lecture question.

questions.question: According to the NIST definition quoted in the lecture, cloud computing enables on-demand network access to a shared pool of what?
questions.explanation: The NIST definition describes cloud computing as convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources. Those resources can include networks, servers, storage, applications, and services that can be provisioned and released with limited management effort. The word “configurable” is important: cloud consumers can obtain resources as needed instead of relying only on fixed hardware or a single resource category.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the essential characteristics of cloud computing as defined by NIST?
questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity means that cloud resources can be provisioned and released quickly as demand changes. A service can scale out during a workload spike and scale back when the demand subsides, often making the available capacity seem very large to the consumer. Manual allocation, mandatory single-tenancy, and fixed billing are not NIST’s defining characteristic in this question; elasticity is about how dynamically resource capacity responds to need.

questions.question: Which cloud deployment model is set up for the exclusive use of a single organization, typically managed on-premises or by a third party off-premises?
questions.explanation: A private cloud is provisioned for the exclusive use of one organization. It may be operated by the organization itself on-premises or managed by a third party off-premises. The key distinction is who the cloud is intended to serve, not simply who owns the hardware or where the servers are located. A public cloud offers services to a broad set of customers, while a community cloud serves organizations with shared requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of a public cloud provider in the lecture?

options.text: A company's internal private data center
A single organization's dedicated server room
A community-only cloud shared by hospitals

questions.explanation: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a public cloud provider, offering computing, storage, networking, and many other services to a broad range of customers. Public-cloud resources are accessed over a network and can be provisioned without the customer owning the underlying data-centre hardware. A company’s internal server room is a private resource, and a cloud reserved for hospitals would fit a different deployment model rather than the general public-cloud example.

questions.question: Which cloud service model provides on-demand delivery of computing infrastructure such as servers, storage, network, and operating system?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides fundamental computing resources such as virtual machines or servers, storage, networking, and often operating-system control. The customer can configure the computing environment while the provider operates the physical infrastructure. SaaS delivers a finished application, and PaaS provides a managed platform for building and running applications. IaaS is therefore the service model that exposes the infrastructure building blocks listed in the question.

questions.question: In the IaaS working methodology, which component allows multiple virtual machines to share the same physical hardware?
questions.explanation: A hypervisor virtualizes physical hardware and allocates its resources among multiple virtual machines. Each VM can run its own operating system and applications while sharing the host computer’s processor, memory, storage, and network interfaces with other VMs. This improves utilization and allows isolated environments to be created on the same server. DNS servers resolve names, load balancers distribute workloads, and firewalls apply traffic rules; they do not perform hardware virtualization.

questions.question: Which cloud service model is described as middleware offered as a service to developers’, removing the need to manage underlying hardware and operating systems?
